Gowarczow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Gowarczów, Poland

Demolished. Gowarczów's Jewish community developed actively from the mid-17th century, with 33 families recorded paying poll taxes in 1662, growing to 46 by 1676 and supporting a synagogue, cheder, mikvah, and cemetery; in 1767, the town's owner Antoni Jabłonowski granted additional trade privileges to the town's Jews, who also developed the local nail industry and iron trade. Jews made up 43.6 percent of the population by 1827, though this share declined to 33.7 percent a century later amid economic collapse and rising antisemitism. During WWII, about a thousand Jews from Gowarczów and its vicinity were deported and murdered at Treblinka. This cemetery, likely established in the mid-17th century before 1662, was enclosed by a well-maintained brick fence as of 1934; its last recorded burial took place in 1942, and the site was later used as a pasture in the 1980s.
